t: Held at Tewodros II's fortress of Maqdala from boyhood, Menelik escaped in 1865, took the kingdom of Shewa in 1866 and after the death of Yohannes IV was crowned emperor on 3 November 1889.

His southern conquests, financed partly by ivory, coffee, gold and a taxed slave trade, brought the Oromo, Wolayta, Gurage and other peoples into the empire, and at Adwa on 1 March 1896 his army defeated Italian colonial forces.

He is regarded as the architect of modern Ethiopia and as a symbol of African resistance to colonialism, while critics among the incorporated peoples, notably the Oromo, accuse him of atrocities, land expropriation and forced assimilation.
dyk: Menelik was named after the legendary Menelik I, son of Solomon and the Queen of Sheba, by his grandfather Sahle Selassie, who is said to have prophesied a reign in which the Ethiopian Empire would be reconstituted.
ev: Sahle Maryam, later Menelik II, is born at Ankober in the kingdom of Shewa
After fighting between Tewodros II and his father's Shewans, the boy is captured and taken to Tewodros's court at Maqdala
Menelik escapes from Maqdala, and in 1866 proclaims himself Negus of Shewa
By the Treaty of Wadara he submits to Emperor Yohannes IV with a stone round his neck and is crowned Negus of Shewa with the Emperor's consent
Shewan forces defeat the emir of Harar at Chelenqo and Harar is annexed
After the death of Yohannes IV he is crowned emperor on Mount Entoto on 3 November
He defeats Italian forces at the Battle of Adwa and Italy recognises Ethiopia's independence by the Treaty of Addis Ababa
Menelik dies after years of paralysis

f.born: 19 August 1844 (or 17 August) in Ankober, Shewa, as Sahle Maryam; son of Haile Melekot, Negus of Shewa, and Ejigayehu; of the Shewan branch of the Solomonic dynasty
f.died: 12 December 1913 (also placed in the night of 12 to 13 December), after strokes from 1906; buried in a mausoleum at the Menelik Palace in Addis Ababa
f.role: King (Negus) of Shewa from 1866 to 1889, quasi-independent from 1878; Emperor of Ethiopia from 1889 until his death in 1913
f.known: the defeat of Italy at the Battle of Adwa in 1896; the southern conquests that took the Ethiopian Empire to its greatest extent; the Treaty of Wuchale and its two versions; the Addis Ababa to Djibouti railway; a cabinet of ministers, schools and a state bank; the atrocities and enslavement associated with the annexations
